title: Weather Alert — Beyond the 956: Tropical Storm In-fa Tracked East of Guam; No Threat Expected, Island at Normal Readiness
excerpt: Tropical Storm In-fa is spinning in the open Pacific about 1,465 miles east of Guam with 40 mph winds — and forecasters say it is no threat to the island. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center's track keeps its closest pass more than 1,000 miles away next Thursday, the National Weather Service in Guam has posted no watch or warning, and Guam remains at Condition of Readiness 4, its normal readiness level, as the island finishes recovering from Super Typhoon Champi.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

WEATHER ALERT — Friday, October 23, 2026 (Saturday, October 24 in Guam)

A new tropical storm named In-fa has formed in the open western Pacific and is being tracked east of Guam — but forecasters say it is no threat to the island. The National Weather Service in Guam has issued no tropical storm or typhoon watch or warning for Guam, and the island remains at Condition of Readiness 4 (COR 4), its normal readiness level, according to the Guam News Network's "Guam Right Now" island conditions page, refreshed Saturday morning, October 24, Chamorro Standard Time.

Where In-fa is now. As of the latest reports out of Guam, Tropical Storm In-fa was centered about 1,465 miles east of Guam, moving southeast at just 1 mph, with maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and gusts to 52 mph, according to the Guam News Network conditions page, which draws on Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and National Weather Service Guam data. The JTWC, which designates the system 30W (In-fa), placed it near 10.6 degrees north latitude and 166.3 degrees east longitude in its Warning #2 — deep in the open Pacific, north of the Marshall Islands and far from any populated island in the Marianas chain.

The forecast keeps it far away. On the JTWC forecast track, In-fa is expected to strengthen over open water and curve through the remote Pacific, making its closest pass to Guam around 4 a.m. Thursday, October 29 (ChST) — still about 1,039 miles to the east of the island, by then as a typhoon with winds of about 138 mph. In other words, even at its closest and strongest, the storm is forecast to pass more than a thousand miles from Guam. The National Weather Service in Guam's latest advisory, issued Saturday, October 24, at 7:58 a.m. ChST, carries no tropical storm or typhoon watch or warning for Guam.

One more disturbance on the board. Forecasters are also monitoring a second disturbance, Invest 97W, about 1,428 miles east of Guam. The JTWC rates its chance of developing into a tropical cyclone within 24 hours as low, according to its October 24, 2026, 7:00 a.m. ChST assessment reported on the Guam News Network conditions page.

Guam stays at normal readiness. Guam's Condition of Readiness 4 — the island's normal, day-to-day readiness posture — was declared in a Guam Homeland Security / Office of Civil Defense (GHS/OCD) release on October 18, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. ChST, and it remains in place. Nothing in the current outlook calls for that to change.

Still finishing the Champi cleanup. The monitoring comes as Guam wraps up its recovery from Super Typhoon Champi, which passed about 10 miles south of the island on October 18. The Guam Power Authority reported on October 22 that the island's power system had reached 99% of its normal load — a recovery In-fa is not expected to interrupt.

Webb Watch 956 will keep tracking JTWC advisories on In-fa and Invest 97W and will update this story if the forecast changes.

Update — October 26, 2026

Typhoon In-fa has strengthened over the open Pacific and is now forecast to pass near or over Pagan Island in the Northern Mariana Islands late Friday as a Category 4 typhoon, according to the National Weather Service in Guam. In its Public Advisory No. 10, issued at 7:00 a.m. Monday (ChST), the weather service put In-fa about 1,270 miles east of Guam and 180 miles northeast of Enewetak, moving northwest at 9 mph, with typhoon-force winds extending up to 15 miles from its center. Forecasters said it could strengthen to Category 2 later Monday and possibly Category 3 by early Tuesday, then track generally west-northwest through the week toward the northern Mariana Islands. Saipan still sat within the southern edge of the cone of uncertainty, and forecasters cautioned that the track and timing could still shift — a shift far enough south could bring the storm very close to Saipan, while a northward shift would take it farther from Pagan and Saipan.

Zoom Earth's tracker, updated at 09:00 UTC on Monday, put In-fa's winds at 215 km/h about 702 km southwest of Wake Island, moving northwest at 7 km/h, with further intensification forecast. No tropical storm or typhoon watches or warnings were in effect for the region as of the weather service advisory. Guam itself remains far from the storm's forecast path, and nothing in the advisory changes Guam's normal readiness posture.

Sources: Guam News Network, "Guam Right Now" island conditions page (refreshed October 24, 2026, 10:48 a.m. ChST); Joint Typhoon Warning Center (assessment of October 24, 2026, 7:00 a.m. ChST; Warning #2 for Tropical Storm 30W (In-fa)); National Weather Service Guam (advisory of October 24, 2026, 7:58 a.m. ChST); Guam Homeland Security / Office of Civil Defense (GHS/OCD); Guam Power Authority; Guam News Network, "Typhoon In-fa forecast to pass near Pagan late this week" (October 26, 2026, citing National Weather Service Guam Public Advisory No. 10); Zoom Earth, Typhoon In-fa tracker (October 26, 2026, 09:00 UTC). Photo: NASA Worldview satellite image (MODIS, Terra), October 24, 2026 — public domain.

Update — October 27, 2026

Typhoon In-fa has strengthened to a Category 3 typhoon and its forecast track has shifted north of the earlier Pagan forecast. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center put In-fa on Tuesday afternoon at 14.3 degrees north, 162.2 degrees east — more than 1,100 miles east of Guam — with sustained winds of 125 mph, moving west-northwest at 2 mph, Isla Public reported, citing the center. The storm remains on track to pass about 180 miles north of Saipan and about 300 miles north of Guam on Friday.

The National Weather Service in Guam, in a Tuesday morning bulletin, put In-fa near 14.1 degrees north, 162.4 degrees east, about 1,180 miles east of Guam, with maximum sustained winds of 125 mph and moving west at just 1 mph, YouWeather reported. Forecasters expect the storm to turn slightly west and pick up forward speed through Wednesday, then turn back to the west-northwest, with intensification beginning Wednesday night and a possible rise to super typhoon strength by Thursday or Friday, though the exact track and intensity remain uncertain. Zoom Earth's tracker, updated at 09:00 UTC on Tuesday, put In-fa's winds at 195 km/h about 717 km southwest of Wake Island, with a forecast peak of 230 km/h within 36 hours. The updated track keeps Guam well south of the forecast Friday pass, and nothing in these updates changes Guam's normal readiness posture.

Sources: Isla Public, "Typhoon In-Fa remains on track to pass north of Saipan on Friday" (October 27, 2026, citing the Joint Typhoon Warning Center); YouWeather, "Typhoon In-fa Intensifies Over the Western Pacific: Northern Mariana Islands Face Potential Threat" (October 27, 2026, citing the National Weather Service in Guam); Zoom Earth, Typhoon In-fa tracker (October 27, 2026, 09:00 UTC).
